correctness.rationale: For each starting phase s, the factor at n=mp+r is U_s^m T_{s,r}. Its two-binomial signature is determined by its ones count and scattered 01 count, and its 01 count equals m q(U_s)+binom(m,2)ab+ma c(T)+q(T). The full-period q(U_s) values on the zero and one branches are integer multiples b and a with exactly g-1 intersections; hence p-g+1 distinct signatures at r=0. For m>binom(p-1,2), any collision requires equal full-period q and equal tail one-count. The only interior r at which a cross-branch equal-q pair has equal prefix one-count yields tails 0^u1^(b-v) versus 1^(b-v)0^u with distinct 01 counts. This proves p signatures for each nonzero residue. The explicit a=2h+1,b=2h+3 witness has full-period q difference 1, tail q difference h(h+2), and collides at m=h(h+2)=p^2/16-1. Independent direct two-binomial signature enumeration verified 1152 stable residue cases a,b<=8, and 24 quadratic-delay witnesses h=1..24. No infinite result is inferred solely from these tests.
